claims.statement: The workspace has seventeen crates under crates/ plus fuzz, grouped into shared contracts, compilation, execution/storage, coordination, external boundaries, and validation/reference tooling rather than a strict dependency ladder; rockstream-cli builds rockstream and rockstream-docgen generates references.
Shared types define weighted Arrow data, epochs, identities, schemas and frontier contracts; selected production kernels are verified, not the entire database.

The live gateway view compiler wraps SQL-lowered PlanNode in a ViewSink and invokes compile_plan_with_strategy; distributed workers deserialize logical plans, compile against shard storage, restore pipeline state, and only then report readiness.
The all role starts embedded control, registers a worker, acquires the normal shard-0 lease, and shares its shard with the gateway instead of creating gateway-shard storage.
A separate gateway opens gateway-shard storage and optionally attaches a DataPlaneClient when configured with control; this does not eliminate gateway-local storage.
The control role attaches persistent shard, topology and migration stores and a frontier aggregator, and enables Raft only when peers are configured.
Workers require a control address, reject deployments whose version, worker identity or lease token differs from current ownership, and recheck the lease fence before persistence.

The frontier role startup branch only creates an in-process aggregator and startup audit/metrics; the old KNOWN_ROLES comment claiming other roles run the embedded node is inconsistent with the current distinct startup branches.

Gateway application traffic uses PostgreSQL wire protocol; worker/control and current DataPlaneClient requests use newline-delimited JSON over TCP, whereas management is a separate version-checked tonic/gRPC service.

In commit_bound_source_ops the gateway serializes shard commits, allocates an epoch, processes a source delta through the compiled pipeline, and batches source mutations, output, operator state and frontier before calling the source runtime commit.

SourceRuntimeCoordinator validates source ownership and lifecycle/epoch consistency, adds source checkpoint, lifecycle and progress to the durable M3 commit, then acknowledges upstream; failed acknowledgement blocks with RS-4016 after local commit and requires checkpoint recovery and acknowledgement retry.
Local view reads reject unpublished backfills and prefer committed compiled output directly from ShardDb rather than waiting for a separately polling ShardReader.

Distributed workers commit output and pipeline state through PhysicalCommitGroup before sending ExecutionProgress; control validates lease/operator identity and acknowledges SourceDeltaCommitted after the expected reports arrive.
Query-time topology refresh opens every configured reader and rejects unavailable topology or unequal durable frontiers; CLI additional query-time shard directories are local-filesystem reader roots.

The distributed materialized-view read branch calls read_workload and merges its snapshot, but the current control ReadWorkload handler supplies shard entries with empty deltas, so this call path alone does not establish serving persisted worker output.
ShardDb commits frontiers with a flush before returning a report, and its durable checkpoints include durably flushed state.

Shared control storage provides cross-process lease-state continuity while Raft term/vote persistence must remain replica-local under storage/raft; private control directories alone do not provide cross-process continuity.

PhysicalCommitGroup bounds retained epochs, bytes and waiters and acknowledges complete epochs after durable flush; legacy GroupCommit only coalesces write fragments and is not the same completion boundary.

The capability matrix is generated from capabilities.toml; Core is release-gated, Maintain supported and Experimental lacks continuity guarantees. Kafka and PostgreSQL CDC sources, exact integer/decimal aggregation and integer equi-joins are Core, while Kafka sink and floating aggregation/joins are Experimental.

ROCKSTREAM_PROJECT_FOCUS.md is a strategic proposal whose connector-reduction amendment overrides older broader connector descriptions; internal object storage for state, checkpoints, spill and recovery and the native PostgreSQL query protocol are explicitly retained, separately from PostgreSQL CDC.

Residual S3/HTTP parser wording and a bindable webhook listener do not imply supported connectors: removed connectors and webhook requests report RS-4017; an older rejection message denies Kafka row export even though the contract records implemented bounded sink delivery as Experimental.

The unified-data-plane test launches the binary and verifies a shard-0 manifest, absence of gateway-shard, and SIGTERM shutdown; distributed_dataplane_process_tests instead uses in-memory simulated lease changes and generation fencing, not a live control-process restart.

The capability ledger attaches named proofs to incremental, backfill, checkpoint recovery, bounded-state and failure behavior rather than treating an operator inventory as sufficient support evidence.
